# Regulatory Capital Minimums Memo — 12 CFR Part 217 (Subpart B, § 217.10)

**Status:** Draft for qualified finance or accounting professional review. This memo is not financial, tax, or investment advice.

**Grounding & Basis Note:** The request refers to "the cited page" without specifying a URL or publication date in the prompt text. This analysis verifies all figures against the official text of 12 CFR Part 217 reproduced in the current eCFR (`ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-217`, `section-217.10`, and `section-217.11`, fetched 2026-11-22) and the 2025 and 2026 Code of Federal Regulations annual editions (`CFR-2025-title12-vol2-part217.xml` and `CFR-2026-title12-vol2-part217.xml`, fetched 2026-11-22). All four sources contain identical text for § 217.10(a)(1). All figures below are dimensionless regulatory ratio percentages (not currency amounts), stated on a regulatory capital basis for the current post-transition period (see historical transition note below).

---

## 1. Minimum Capital Ratios (Before Buffers or Other Add-Ons)

Under **12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)**, before applying any capital conservation buffer, stress capital buffer, countercyclical capital buffer, GSIB surcharge, or leverage buffer under § 217.11, a Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:

| Capital Ratio | Minimum Requirement | Unit / Currency | Basis | Exact Regulatory Citation |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio** | **4.5** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory capital / risk-weighted assets (standardized, or lower of standardized and advanced approaches) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(i) |
| **Tier 1 capital ratio** | **6** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory capital / risk-weighted assets (standardized, or lower of standardized and advanced approaches) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(ii) |
| **Total capital ratio** | **8** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory capital / risk-weighted assets (standardized, or lower of standardized and advanced approaches) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(iii) |
| **Leverage ratio** | **4** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory Tier 1 leverage measure (non-risk-weighted) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(iv) |

### Additional Conditional Minimum in § 217.10(a)(1)
- **Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) — 3 percent** (`12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(v)`): Applicable **only** to "advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions or, for Category III Board-regulated institutions." While not one of the four general ratios named in the request, it appears in the same § 217.10(a)(1) list of base minimum capital ratios.

---

## 2. Ratio Calculation Bases & Institutional Applicability in § 217.10

- **Standardized Capital Ratio Calculations (`12 CFR § 217.10(b)`):**
  - *CET1 capital ratio (`§ 217.10(b)(1)`):* CET1 capital divided by **standardized total risk-weighted assets**.
  - *Tier 1 capital ratio (`§ 217.10(b)(2)`):* Tier 1 capital divided by **standardized total risk-weighted assets**.
  - *(Note: Standardized total capital and leverage ratio mechanics are cross-referenced via `§ 217.11(a)` to `§ 217.10(b)(3)` and `(c)`.)*
- **Advanced Approaches Capital Ratio Calculations (`12 CFR § 217.10(d)`):**
  - Once an advanced approaches Board-regulated institution completes the parallel run process and receives Board notification under `§ 217.121(d)`, its CET1 (`§ 217.10(d)(1)`), Tier 1 (`§ 217.10(d)(2)`), and Total Capital (`§ 217.10(d)(3)`) ratios are each the **lower of**:
    1. The respective capital divided by **standardized total risk-weighted assets**; and
    2. The respective capital divided by **advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets**.
- **Community Bank Leverage Ratio (CBLR) Framework (`12 CFR § 217.10(a)(2)`):**
  - A qualifying community banking organization (as defined in `§ 217.12`) that is subject to the CBLR framework is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in `§ 217.10(a)`.
- **Insurance Depository Institution Holding Companies (`12 CFR § 217.10(f)(1)`):**
  - An insurance bank holding company or insurance savings and loan holding company that is a state-regulated insurer and subject to subpart J of Part 217 is not required to meet the risk-based minimum capital ratio requirements in `§ 217.10(a)(1)(i)–(iii)`.
- **General Capital Adequacy Requirement (`12 CFR § 217.10(e)`):**
  - Notwithstanding the numerical minimums, a Board-regulated institution must maintain capital commensurate with the level and nature of all risks to which it is exposed (`§ 217.10(e)(1)`) and maintain an internal capital adequacy assessment process and strategy (`§ 217.10(e)(2)`).

---

## 3. Buffers and Add-Ons Excluded per Constraint (12 CFR § 217.11)

To confirm the boundary between the base minimums and "capital buffers or other add-ons," `12 CFR § 217.11` layers payout-limiting buffers on top of the `§ 217.10(a)` minimums (specifically computing buffers as actual capital ratios *minus* the `§ 217.10(a)` minimum requirements). Per the request constraint, the following § 217.11 add-ons are **excluded** from the 4.5% / 6% / 8% / 4% minimums above:
- **Capital Conservation Buffer / Stress Capital Buffer Requirement (`§ 217.11(a)`):** For institutions subject to `12 CFR 225.8` or `238.170`, composed solely of CET1 capital (with a 2.5% default stress capital buffer requirement if not yet assigned).
- **Countercyclical Capital Buffer (`§ 217.11(b)(2)(iii)`):** Adjustable by the Board between 0% and 2.5% of risk-weighted assets for U.S. credit exposures.
- **GSIB Surcharge (`§ 217.11(d)`):** Calculated under subpart H for global systemically important BHCs.
- **Leverage Buffer (`§ 217.11(c)(4)`, `§ 217.11(f)`):** Composed solely of Tier 1 capital, measured as the supplementary leverage ratio minus 3% for GSIB BHCs and their state member bank subsidiaries (with the state member bank leverage buffer requirement equal to the lesser of 1.0% or 50% of the parent GSIB's method 1 surcharge under `§ 217.403(b)`).

---

## 4. Reviewer Verification Check: Historical Transition Provision (§ 217.300)

Because the prompt did not include the exact link to "the cited page," the reviewer should confirm that the cited page reproduces the current/post-2015 Part 217 rule (`§ 217.10(a)(1)`). Under the historical transition provisions in **`12 CFR § 217.300`**, for the **January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014** transition period only, the minimum ratios were **4 percent CET1**, **5.5 percent Tier 1**, **8 percent total capital**, and **4 percent leverage**. All current and 2025–2026 CFR editions of `§ 217.10(a)(1)` state **4.5 percent CET1**, **6 percent Tier 1**, **8 percent total capital**, and **4 percent leverage**.

*Notice: This output is a reference draft prepared for review by a qualified finance, actuarial, or regulatory professional. It does not constitute legal, regulatory, financial, tax, or investment advice.*

---

#### 1. Summary of Required Figures

| Ask | Parameter | Value in Original Text | Unit / Basis / Period / Currency | Authoritative Source in Original Text |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **2** | **Probability (Confidence Level)** | **99.5%** (printed as `99,5 %`) | Unit: `%` (probability / VaR confidence level). Basis: Regulatory VaR of basic own funds / probability of meeting obligations. Period: One-year risk horizon. Currency: N/A (dimensionless). | Directive 2009/138/EC (as adopted 25 Nov 2009), **Article 101(3)** & **Recital (64)** |
| **2** | **Time Horizon** | **One-year period** (with new business expected over the **following 12 months**) | Unit: `year` (`1 year` / `12 months`). Basis: Going-concern calibration horizon for unexpected losses on existing business and expected new business. Currency: N/A. | Directive 2009/138/EC (as adopted 25 Nov 2009), **Article 101(3)** |
| **3** | **Equivalent Ruin Frequency** | **Once in every 200 cases** (1-in-200) | Unit: `cases` (stated verbatim as `once in every 200 cases`; corresponds to a 200-year return period given the one-year horizon in Art. 101(3)). Basis: Economic capital threshold. Currency: N/A. | Directive 2009/138/EC (as adopted 25 Nov 2009), **Recital (64)** |

---

#### 2. Verbatim Citations from the Original Adopted Text (25 November 2009)

Source: *Directive 2009/138/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of Insurance and Reinsurance (Solvency II) (recast)*, Original English Official Journal / As-adopted PDF (`eudr_20090138_adopted_en.pdf`).

1. **Article 101(3) — Calculation of the Solvency Capital Requirement** (Title I, Chapter VI, Section 4, Subsection 1):
   > "The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calibrated so as to ensure that all quantifiable risks to which an insurance or reinsurance undertaking is exposed are taken into account. It shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months. With respect to existing business, it shall cover only unexpected losses.
   > 
   > It shall correspond to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period."

2. **Recital (64) — Equivalent Probability and Ruin Frequency**:
   > "(64) In order to promote good risk management and align regulatory capital requirements with industry practices, the Solvency Capital Requirement should be determined as the economic capital to be held by insurance and reinsurance undertakings in order to ensure that ruin occurs no more often than once in every 200 cases or, alternatively, that those undertakings will still be in a position, with a probability of at least 99,5 %, to meet their obligations to policy [holders and beneficiaries...]"

*(Note for completeness: Under **Article 122(1)**, undertakings using an internal model may use a different time period or risk measure than Article 101(3) provided the resulting outputs yield an equivalent level of protection for policyholders and beneficiaries.)*

---

#### 3. Arithmetic Reconciliation of Confidence Level and Ruin Frequency

- **Stated confidence level ($p$):** $99.5\% = 0.995$ (Source: Article 101(3); Recital (64)).
- **Implied one-year ruin / exceedance probability ($1 - p$):**
  $$1 - 0.995 = 0.005 = 0.5\%$$
- **Equivalent ruin frequency (return period):**
  $$\frac{1}{1 - 0.995} = \frac{1}{0.005} = 200$$
- **Reconciliation to Recital (64):** A $0.5\%$ probability of exceedance equals $1$ event per $200$ cases, matching the Directive's exact wording in Recital (64) ("ruin occurs no more often than once in every 200 cases"). Combined with the "one-year period" specified in Article 101(3), this represents an expected ruin frequency of no more than once every 200 years.

  25% (the main rate).
  - Period: Financial Years starting 1 April 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026 (1 April 2023 onwards).

  - Source: HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (updated 1 April 2026).

  Companies with profits between £50,000 (the Marginal Relief lower limit) and £250,000 (the Marginal Relief upper limit) are charged Corporation Tax at the 25% main rate, reduced by Marginal Relief using HMRC's standard fraction of 3/200 (0.015 or 1.5%). This produces a gradual increase in the effective Corporation Tax rate from 19% at £50,000 to 25% at £250,000.
  - Period: Financial Years starting 1 April 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026.
  - Currency & Basis: GBP (£); non-ring fence profits for a standalone company with a 12-month accounting period.
  - Source: HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (updated 1 April 2026) and *Marginal Relief for Corporation Tax* (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/corporation-tax-marginal-relief).

Source: HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (updated 1 April 2026).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Assumed Basis for Illustration: Standalone company (0 associated companies), 12-month accounting period wholly within FY 2023 to FY 2026, non-ring fence profits, GBP (£), with augmented profits equal to total taxable profits (i.e. no exempt qualifying distributions).

- Marginal Relief: (£250,000 - £50,000) x (3 / 200) = £200,000 x 0.015 = £3,000

2. STATUTORY AND REGULATORY TEXT ANALYSIS (12 CFR PART 3)
A. Who 12 CFR Part 3 Binds Directly (§ 3.10)
Under 12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1) (78 FR 62157, 62273, Oct. 11, 2013, as maintained in CFR-2026-title12-vol1-part3-subpartB.html and eCFR), the minimum capital ratios are imposed expressly on a "national bank or Federal savings association":
- Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio: 4.5% (12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(i); basis: CET1 capital under § 3.20(b) divided by total risk-weighted assets, taking the lower of standardized RWA and, if applicable, advanced approaches RWA per § 3.10(b)(1) and § 3.10(c)(1)).
- Tier 1 capital ratio: 6.0% (12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(ii); basis: Tier 1 capital / RWA).
- Total capital ratio: 8.0% (12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(iii); basis: Total capital / RWA).
- Leverage ratio: 4.0% (12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(iv); basis: Tier 1 capital / average total consolidated assets).
- Supplementary leverage ratio: 3.0% for Category III or advanced approaches OCC-regulated institutions (12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(v); basis: Tier 1 capital / total leverage exposure under § 3.10(c)(2)).
- Tangible capital ratio: 1.5% for Federal savings associations only (12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(vi); basis: core capital / average total assets under § 3.10(d)(4)).

B. Capital Conservation Buffer and Countercyclical Buffer (§ 3.11) — Not a Direct Branch Floor
For national banks and Federal savings associations, 12 CFR § 3.11 imposes payout limitations unless the institution maintains a capital conservation buffer above its § 3.10(a)(1) minimums:
- Minimum CET1 + full Capital Conservation Buffer (no payout limitation): 4.5% (§ 3.10(a)(1)(i)) + 2.5% (§ 3.11(a)(4)) = 7.0% of RWA.
- With Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB) (§ 3.11(b), 0% to 2.5% of RWA, effective 12 months after OCC announcement unless an earlier date is stated): 4.5% + 2.5% + (0.0% to 2.5%) = 7.0% to 9.5% of RWA.
Note: These buffer thresholds likewise apply to a "national bank or Federal savings association," not to a Federal branch.

C. Why 12 CFR Part 3 Imposes No Direct CET1 Ratio on a Federal Branch
1. Legal Entity Distinction: A Federal branch of a foreign bank is an unincorporated U.S. office of a foreign bank licensed by the OCC under the International Banking Act of 1978 (12 U.S.C. § 3102), not a separately chartered national bank or Federal savings association with its own common stock, retained earnings, or standalone CET1 capital.
2. Distinction in 12 CFR § 3.2: Section 3.2 defines "Foreign bank" by cross-reference to 12 CFR § 211.2 (Regulation K), explicitly noting "(other than a depository institution)," and references "home country supervisor" standards for foreign banks rather than applying Part 3 CET1 floors to foreign bank branches.

Because this falls outside the direct text of 12 CFR Part 3, a qualified reviewer should confirm the applicable regime under separate statutory and regulatory authorities:
- OCC Capital Equivalency Deposit (CED): Federal branches are subject to OCC asset-maintenance and Capital Equivalency Deposit requirements (12 U.S.C. § 3102(g); 12 CFR Part 28, Subpart B, including § 28.15), rather than Part 3 risk-based CET1 ratios.

- OCC Reservation of Authority: Under 12 CFR Part 3 and supervisory authority, the OCC retains case-by-case supervisory authority over individual institutions, though no general rule in Part 3 imposes a direct CET1 ratio on a Federal branch.

- Entity Type: National bank or Federal savings association (reference benchmark only) | Applicable Rule: 12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(i) | Direct CET1 Minimum Ratio: 4.5% | Buffer (§ 3.11): +2.5% CCB (+0.0% to 2.5% CCyB) = 7.0% to 9.5% | Basis: CET1 capital (§ 3.20(b)) / total RWA (§ 3.10(b)(1), (c)(1)); period as in force 2026-11-21.

answer:
MEMORANDUM — DRAFT FOR PROFESSIONAL REVIEW
To: Finance & Accounting Team / Compliance Lead
From: Privacy Counsel
Date: 2026-11-23 (Assessing Regulation in Force as of 2026-11-21)
Subject: Scoping of Annual Privacy Notice Obligation under 17 CFR Part 248, Subpart A (Companies and Business-Purpose Individuals)

DISCLAIMER: This memorandum is a draft prepared for review by a qualified finance, accounting, or legal/compliance professional. It does not constitute legal, financial, tax, or investment advice. No monetary figures, balances, or financial calculations are presented; the analysis addresses regulatory scope as of 2026-11-21 based on the cited federal regulatory text.

1. EXECUTIVE VERDICT
Verdict (Ask 2): No.
Apart from 17 CFR § 248.30(b), 17 CFR Part 248, Subpart A as in force on 2026-11-21 does NOT cover information about companies or information about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for business (commercial or agricultural) purposes. Consequently, the annual privacy notice requirement in § 248.5 (and related initial, revised, and opt-out notice provisions in Subpart A) does not apply to such information.

2. REGIME CLARIFICATION
Note on nomenclature: The project framing refers to "Regulation P," which is commonly used for the CFPB's privacy rule at 12 CFR Part 1016. Title 17 CFR Part 248, Subpart A is the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) Regulation S-P ("Subpart A—Regulation S-P: Privacy of Consumer Financial Information and Safeguarding Personal Information (§§ 248.1 - 248.31-248.100)", 17 CFR Part 248, 65 FR 40362, June 29, 2000; nomenclature changes at 74 FR 40431, Aug. 11, 2009). This analysis addresses 17 CFR Part 248, Subpart A as requested.

3. SOURCED REGULATORY ANALYSIS
A. Controlling Scope and Exclusion Text (§ 248.1(b))
The fetched eCFR text of 17 CFR Part 248, Subpart A (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-248/subpart-A, fetched 2026-11-23T00:12:28Z, sha256 d91a3c8df350) establishes two direct, dispositive rules in § 248.1(b):
- Positive Scope Limit: "Except with respect to § 248.30(b), this subpart applies only to nonpublic personal information about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for personal, family, or household purposes from the institutions listed below."
- Express Exclusion: "This subpart does not apply to information about companies or about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for business, commercial, or agricultural purposes."

B. Relevant Definitions and Annual Notice Linkage (§§ 248.3, 248.4, 248.5)
- "Company" (§ 248.3(f)): Defined as "any corporation, limited liability company, business trust, general or limited partnership, association, or similar organization." Entities meeting this definition are expressly excluded from Subpart A (apart from § 248.30(b)).
- "Consumer" (§ 248.3(g)(1)): Defined as "an individual who obtains or has obtained a financial product or service from you that is to be used primarily for personal, family, or household purposes, or that individual's legal representative." Individuals obtaining products or services primarily for business, commercial, or agricultural purposes are not "consumers."
- "Customer" and Annual Notice (§§ 248.4(c)(1), 248.5(a)): A customer relationship is established only when the institution and a "consumer" enter into a continuing relationship (§ 248.4(c)(1)). The annual privacy notice requirement in § 248.5(a) mandates clear and conspicuous notice "to customers... not less than annually during the continuation of the customer relationship." Because neither companies nor business-purpose individuals qualify as "consumers," they cannot become "customers" triggering § 248.5(a).
- Interaction with § 248.5(e) Exception: For covered personal-purpose customers, § 248.5(e)(1) provides an exception from annual notice delivery if nonpublic personal information is shared with nonaffiliated third parties only under §§ 248.13, 248.14, or 248.15 and disclosure policies under § 248.6(a)(2)–(5) and (9) have not changed. For companies and business-purpose individuals, the institution does not need to rely on § 248.5(e) because the accounts fall outside Subpart A altogether under § 248.1(b).

C. Reason for the § 248.30(b) Carve-Out
Section 248.1(b) carves out § 248.30(b) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-248/subpart-A/subject-group-ECFR931661bf1d834f8/section-248.30, fetched 2026-11-23T00:12:27Z, sha256 6416855f3c7b). Under § 248.30(b), covered institutions (other than notice-registered broker-dealers) must properly dispose of "consumer information" and "customer information," and § 248.30(d)(1)(i) defines "consumer information" to include consumer reports (or records derived therefrom) about an individual maintained or possessed "for a business purpose." Because Ask 1 expressly excludes § 248.30(b), this disposal obligation does not affect the negative verdict on annual privacy notices and the remainder of Subpart A.

4. SCOPING & COMPLIANCE IMPLEMENTATION NOTES FOR REVIEW
1. Threshold Institution Status (§ 248.1(b)): Confirm the institution is a financial institution subject to Subpart A (SEC-registered broker, dealer, investment company, or investment adviser, etc.). Note that § 248.1(b) also states: "This subpart does not apply to foreign (non-resident) brokers, dealers, investment companies and investment advisers that are not registered with the Commission."
2. Edge Cases — Sole Proprietors and Mixed-Purpose Accounts: Where an individual (such as a sole proprietor or high-net-worth individual) opens an account with both business and personal characteristics, document the primary purpose of the financial product or service. If obtained "primarily" for personal, family, or household purposes, the individual is a "consumer" (and potentially a "customer") covered by Subpart A's notice rules; if obtained "primarily" for business, commercial, or agricultural purposes, it is excluded.
3. Effective-Date Basis (2026-11-21 vs. 2026-11-23 Fetch): The eCFR sources cited above were fetched on 2026-11-23 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-248, fetched 2026-11-23T00:12:28Z, sha256 b1e9528b3e2b; https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/part-248, fetched 2026-11-23T00:12:27Z, sha256 5532df643700). Qualified compliance counsel should confirm no Federal Register amendment to § 248.1(b) or § 248.5 took effect specifically on 2026-11-22 or 2026-11-23 that would alter the text as in force on 2026-11-21.
4. Other Regimes: Exclusion from Subpart A's annual notice scope does not exempt business-purpose or entity records from § 248.30(b) disposal rules (where applicable), Regulation S-AM (Subpart B), Regulation S-ID (Subpart C), state privacy statutes, or contractual confidentiality commitments.

answer:
DRAFT FOR QUALIFIED FINANCE OR ACCOUNTING PROFESSIONAL REVIEW ONLY. This memorandum is prepared by Regulatory Counsel and does not constitute financial, tax, or investment advice.

1. EXECUTIVE CONCLUSION
Under the original text of Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2015 on payment services in the internal market (PSD2; OJ L 337, 23.12.2015), an authorised EU payment institution providing solely the payment service in point (6) of Annex I (money remittance) must maintain a statutory minimum capital floor of EUR 20,000 at all times (period: continuous from authorisation; currency: EUR; basis: regulatory initial capital / own funds floor under Articles 7(a) and 8(1) of Directive (EU) 2015/2366). At all times after authorisation, its ongoing own funds must equal or exceed the higher of EUR 20,000 or the activity-based own-funds requirement calculated under Article 9 (Methods A, B, or C, as designated by the home Member State's competent authorities).

2. STATUTORY BASIS AND GROUNDING NOTE
- Directive identified: Directive (EU) 2015/2366, adopted at Strasbourg on 25 November 2015 (confirmed in retrieved source text).
- Annex I service classification: Point (6) of Annex I covers 'Money remittance' (defined in Article 4(22) as a payment service where funds are received from a payer, without any payment accounts being created in the name of the payer or the payee, for the sole purpose of transferring a corresponding amount to a payee or to another payment service provider acting on behalf of the payee, and/or where such funds are received on behalf of and made available to the payee).
- Grounding note on retrieved excerpts: The harness-retrieved text excerpts confirm the directive's adoption date (25 November 2015), the Section 1 ('General rules') structure for payment institutions, and the Article 32(1)(a) small-payment-institution exemption ceiling of EUR 3,000,000 monthly average transaction value for points (1) to (6) of Annex I. The specific capital amounts and formulas in Articles 7, 8, and 9 and the text of Annex I point (6) are stated directly from the original text of Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (OJ L 337, 23.12.2015) and should be cross-checked against the official OJ publication during professional review.

3. CAPITAL REQUIREMENT SCHEDULE AND ARITHMETIC
(a) Initial Capital Floor — Article 7(a)
- Figure: EUR 20,000
- Source: Directive (EU) 2015/2366, Title II, Chapter 1, Section 1, Article 7(a).
- Period / Currency / Basis: At the time of authorisation and at no time less than EUR 20,000 (ongoing); EUR; initial capital comprising one or more of the Common Equity Tier 1 items referred to in Article 26(1)(a) to (e) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 (CRR).
- Statutory rule: 'where the payment institution provides only the payment service referred to in point (6) of Annex I, its capital shall at no time be less than EUR 20 000'. (By contrast, Article 7(b) requires EUR 50,000 for point (7) payment initiation services, and Article 7(c) requires EUR 125,000 for any of points (1) to (5).)

(b) Ongoing Minimum Own Funds Requirement — Article 8(1)
- Arithmetic rule: Required Own Funds (t) = max(Initial Capital under Art. 7(a), Own Funds under Art. 9)
- Floor check: Because Initial Capital under Art. 7(a) = EUR 20,000, Required Own Funds (t) = max(EUR 20,000, Own Funds under Art. 9) >= EUR 20,000.
- Source: Directive (EU) 2015/2366, Article 8(1).
- Period / Currency / Basis: At all times on an ongoing basis; EUR; own funds as defined in point (118) of Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, subject to Article 8(2) (anti-double-gearing) and optional Article 8(3) consolidated-supervision waiver.

(c) Activity-Based Own Funds Calculation — Article 9 (Applied if > EUR 20,000)
Where the home Member State's competent authorities apply Method A, B, or C under Article 9(1), the analyst must compute the applicable method and take max(EUR 20,000, Method Result):

1. Method A (Fixed Overheads — Article 9(1), Method A):
   - Formula: Own Funds_A = 10% x Fixed Overheads_(t-1)
   - Period / Currency / Basis: Preceding financial year fixed overheads (or business-plan projection if operating < 1 year); EUR; regulatory own funds.
   - Threshold breakeven arithmetic: EUR 20,000 / 0.10 = EUR 200,000. Method A governs above the floor when Fixed Overheads_(t-1) > EUR 200,000.

2. Method B (Payment Volume — Article 9(1), Method B & Article 9(2)(a)):
   - Let PV = (1 / 12) x Total Payment Transactions Executed_(t-1) (preceding 12 months / preceding year; EUR; gross payment volume).
   - Scaling factor k = 0.5 (Article 9(2)(a), applicable where the institution provides only the service in point (6) of Annex I).
   - Formula: Own Funds_B = 0.5 x [4.0% x min(PV, EUR 5,000,000) + 2.5% x max(0, min(PV, EUR 10,000,000) - EUR 5,000,000) + 1.0% x max(0, min(PV, EUR 100,000,000) - EUR 10,000,000) + 0.5% x max(0, min(PV, EUR 250,000,000) - EUR 100,000,000) + 0.25% x max(0, PV - EUR 250,000,000)].
   - Threshold breakeven arithmetic: At PV = EUR 1,000,000 (annual payment volume = 12 x EUR 1,000,000 = EUR 12,000,000), Own Funds_B = 0.5 x (0.04 x EUR 1,000,000) = 0.5 x EUR 40,000 = EUR 20,000. Method B exceeds the EUR 20,000 floor when PV > EUR 1,000,000.

3. Method C (Relevant Indicator — Article 9(1), Method C & Article 9(2)(a)):
   - Let RI = Interest Income + Interest Expenses + Commissions and Fees Received + Other Operating Income (preceding financial year; EUR; audited/accounting basis per Article 9(1)).
   - Scaling factor k = 0.5 (Article 9(2)(a), for point (6) only).
   - Formula: Own Funds_C = 0.5 x [10% x min(RI, EUR 2,500,000) + 8% x max(0, min(RI, EUR 5,000,000) - EUR 2,500,000) + 6% x max(0, min(RI, EUR 25,000,000) - EUR 5,000,000) + 3% x max(0, min(RI, EUR 50,000,000) - EUR 25,000,000) + 1.5% x max(0, RI - EUR 50,000,000)].
   - Threshold breakeven arithmetic: At RI = EUR 400,000, Own Funds_C = 0.5 x (0.10 x EUR 400,000) = 0.5 x EUR 40,000 = EUR 20,000. Method C exceeds the EUR 20,000 floor when RI > EUR 400,000.

4. SCOPE BOUNDARIES AND ROLE LIMITATIONS
- Small Payment Institution Derogation (Article 32(1)(a)): Member States may waive Section 1 requirements (including Articles 7–9) where the preceding 12 months' monthly average total value of payment transactions does not exceed a national limit of at most EUR 3,000,000 (period: preceding 12 months; currency: EUR; basis: transaction volume). Because the prompt specifies an authorised EU payment institution under full directive rules (and provides no Article 32 exemption or Member State waiver), the EUR 20,000 floor under Articles 7(a) and 8(1) governs.
- Outside Regulatory Counsel Scope (Directive Text Analysis): Determining whether the institution's actual ongoing requirement exceeds EUR 20,000 requires entity-level financial statement inputs (fixed overheads, annual payment volume, or relevant indicator) and verification of which Article 9 method and national transposition rules apply in the entity's home Member State, as well as any local-currency conversion rules for non-eurozone Member States.

COMPLIANCE REVIEW MEMORANDUM — EMIR ORIGINAL TEXT (REGULATION (EU) NO 648/2012)

Notice and Scope: Output is a draft for a qualified finance or accounting professional to review. It is not financial, tax, investment, or legal advice. All figures and deadlines below are stated on the basis of the original English-language Official Journal text of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 as adopted in 2012 (prior to subsequent amendments such as EMIR Refit). Currency is not applicable (the figures are regulatory time periods rather than monetary amounts), and no arithmetic is involved because the durations are stated directly in the statutory text.

1. Reporting Deadline for Derivative Contracts (Ask 2)
- Requirement: 1 working day following the conclusion, modification, or termination of the contract ("no later than the working day following").
- Source: Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 (as originally adopted), Article 9(1).
- Basis & Period: Applicable to derivative contracts entered into before 16 August 2012 and remaining outstanding on that date, and contracts entered into on or after 16 August 2012 (Article 9(1)(a)-(b)). Note that Article 9(6)(b) also mandated ESMA to develop draft implementing technical standards by 30 September 2012 specifying the reporting start date and any phase-in for pre-existing contracts.
- Verbatim Text (Article 9(1), first subparagraph): "Counterparties and CCPs shall ensure that the details of any derivative contract they have concluded and of any modification or termination of the contract are reported to a trade repository registered in accordance with Article 55 or recognised in accordance with Article 77. The details shall be reported no later than the working day following the conclusion, modification or termination of the contract."
- Related Operational Rules (Article 9(1), 9(3)-(4)): Counterparties and CCPs may delegate reporting and must ensure details are reported without duplication (Article 9(1)). Where no trade repository is available, details must be reported to ESMA (Article 9(3)). Reporting in accordance with these obligations does not breach contractual or statutory disclosure restrictions and confers no liability on the reporting entity or its directors or employees (Article 9(4)).

2. Record Retention Period for Counterparties (Ask 3)
- Requirement: At least 5 years following the termination of the contract.
- Source: Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 (as originally adopted), Article 9(2).
- Basis & Period: Applies to counterparties for any derivative contract concluded and any modification thereto; the 5-year minimum retention clock runs post-termination (meaning records must effectively be maintained throughout the life of the contract plus at least 5 years after termination).
- Verbatim Text (Article 9(2)): "Counterparties shall keep a record of any derivative contract they have concluded and any modification for at least five years following the termination of the contract."

3. Compliance Review Notes
- Temporal Limitation: This analysis strictly reflects Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 as originally adopted in 2012. Subsequent EU amending regulations and national/UK onshored versions have modified EMIR reporting and operational rules over time; current compliance procedures must be verified against the consolidated legislation in force in the relevant jurisdiction.
- Cross-Reference Note: Under the original 2012 text, both the reporting deadline and the counterparty record-retention requirement sit in Article 9 (paragraphs 1 and 2, respectively).
